title: SLO Sherpa: 90-day Cross-Functional Onboarding & Activation Canvas
body:
Purpose
---
This is a working canvas to guide the first 90 days of cross-functional activation for the Reliability Program (SLOs + runbooks + telemetry). Intended audience: feature/product owners, platform, SRE, Observability, and Release Engineering. The doc is intentionally pragmatic — sketchy checklists, meeting rhythms, and small experiments we can complete in a quarter.

Executive summary (one-line)
---
Kick off a repeatable, low-friction SLO onboarding pipeline for 8 pilot services, with automated fidelity checks, a lightweight runbook template, and a stakeholder cadence to reduce service-level incidents and shorten MTTx by month 3.

Goals & success signals (quarterly)
---
- Goal 1: Define and publish SLOs for 8 pilot services (2 infra, 6 product)
  - Success signal: SLOs live in Confluence + tracked in SLO dashboard; 8/8 entries with owner and SLIs.
- Goal 2: Create lightweight runbooks for critical user flows for each pilot
  - Success: Runbooks tested in a simulated incident tabletop for 6/8 services.
- Goal 3: Reduce P99 latency throttles and pager noise
  - Success: Pager volume down 25% vs baseline; P99 request latency improvement for two high-volume endpoints.
- Goal 4: Provide a repeatable SLO checklist and CI gate (evaluation harness)
  - Success: At least one PR demonstrating automated SLO smoke tests (PLAT-4872) merged.

Scope (what is in / out)
---
In: onboarding pipeline for 8 pilots, telemetry instrumentation gaps, runbook templates, stakeholder rituals, risk register, simple canary gating.
Out: universal rollout to entire org (this is a follow-up phase), major refactors of core telemetry systems (only targeted small instrumentation changes).

Stakeholders & roles (initial)
---
- SRE lead (owner): Priya Raman — program lead, escalation coordinator
- Observability: Liam Chen — dashboards, alert tuning, query templates
- Platform/Runtime: Marco Ricci — deploy hooks, canary guardrails
- Product/Feature reps: Sofia Martinez (Search), Noah Patel (Chat), Evelyn Brooks (Embeddings) — define user journeys and SLO targets
- Release Eng: TBD — assist with rollout automation and CI gates
- Customer Success: optional consult for customer-impact mapping

90-day plan (high level)
---
Weeks 1–2 (Discover + Align)
- Kickoff working session: who, why, initial scope (30–60 min).
- Triage pool of candidate services; pick 8 pilots (license: 2 infra, 6 product).
- Inventory: current SLIs/dashboard availability (observability sweep).
- Output: Pilot roster, owner matrix, initial meeting cadence.

Weeks 3–6 (Instrument + Draft SLOs)
- Implement missing SLIs for critical flows (small PRs, prioritized).
- Draft SLOs with product owners — prefer availability/latency per primary user journey.
- Create Confluence SLO page for each pilot with: objective, indicators, measurement window, burn rate thresholds.
- Run a quick baseline measurement (7-day window) for realistic targets.

Weeks 7–10 (Runbooks + Canary Workflows)
- Draft lightweight runbooks (template below) and sync with oncall reps.
- Implement canary guardrails for model-serving endpoints (rate limit, fallback route).
- Create CI smoke test that validates SLO page metadata and that the SLI query executes (linked to PLAT-4872).

Weeks 11–13 (Tabletop + Fixes)
- Run 2 tabletop incident exercises, one infra-facing and one product-facing.
- Capture gaps in runbooks and telemetry; implement the top-5 quick fixes.
- Retrospective and decision: scale plan vs more pilots.

Artifacts & templates
---
1) Minimal SLO page (Confluence): title, owner, user-journey, SLI query, measurement window, SLO target, alert thresholds, linked runbook, linked PRs/Jira.
2) Runbook template (lightweight): symptoms, likely causes, quick mitigation steps (5 lines), escalations, postmortem owner.
3) SLO smoke test: small script that queries SLI and validates presence of required metadata.
4) Oncall tabletop script: scenario, inject, expected mitigations, checklist.

Runbook quick template (copyable)
---
- Title: [service] — [flow]
- Symptoms: short bullet list
- Triage quick checks (3): health endpoints, queue depth, recent deploy ID
- Fast mitigation (2): temporary restart pattern, traffic reroute
- Owner/escalation: oncall -> SRE lead (Priya) -> Platform lead (Marco)
- Postmortem link: (placeholder)

Rituals & meetings
---
- Weekly 30m sync (SRE + Observability + product owners) — progress, blockers, burn-down.
- Biweekly tabletop / exercise (one pilot per meeting) — invite oncall and product lead.
- Monthly steering 45m (Heads of SRE, Observability, Platform, Product) — review metrics and decide scaling.
- Slack channel: #reliability-sherpa (for async updates)

Metrics & dashboards (initial)
---
- SLI coverage: percent of pilots with complete SLI queries. Baseline goal: 100% by week 6.
- Pager volume per service (weekly trend).
- Burn-rate alerts fired (count, per service).
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) measured in tabletop & real incidents.

Risk register (top items)
---
- Risk: owners are overloaded; mitigation: limit to 8 pilots, offer dev time credits.
- Risk: telemetry queries are slow or unreliable; mitigation: create sampling flag for test runs + short-term dashboards.
- Risk: runbooks are ignored; mitigation: mandatory tabletop signoff to mark a runbook as validated.

Mini experiments (to run quickly)
---
1) SLO smoke test as a GitHub Action: small action that checks SLO page metadata on PRs. (PR example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/821)
2) Prefix KV caching experiment for search endpoint to measure P99 impact (two-week A/B).
3) Alert dedupe script to reduce duplicate paging for the same root cause (measure pager count before/after).

Checklist for pilot onboarding (per service)
---
- [ ] Identify product owner and designate SLI owner
- [ ] Confirm primary user journey and golden metric (latency or availability)
- [ ] SLI implemented with query + baseline measurement
- [ ] SLO page created and linked in dashboard
- [ ] Runbook drafted and assigned
- [ ] Tabletop scheduled and executed
- [ ] CI smoke test added to relevant repo

Open questions & decisions (needs answers this sprint)
---
- What is the canonical measurement window we adopt org-wide (30d vs 14d)? Recommendation: 30d for stability, 7d for quick pilot baselining — decision requested by Nov 20.
- Who will own PR gating enforcement for SLO smoke tests? (Platform or SRE?)
- Do we require legal/cust-success review for SLO language on customer-facing pages?

Notes to self / loose thoughts
---
- Keep runbooks one screen — people won't read long pages.
- Prefer narrower SLOs that map to a clear business metric (search-relevance latency).
- Use tabletop failures to make runbooks real: inject deliberate small failures during normal hours.

Next steps (this week)
---
- Schedule kickoff (Priya) and invite product reps (Sofia, Noah, Evelyn) — target: within 3 business days.
- Run initial observability sweep (Liam) and publish pilot roster.
- Create a repo template for SLO smoke test and open PR.

---

- 2025-12-08: Added runbook template and canary guardrail notes.

---
